entries.subject: Photometric law for the lighting overlays
entries.finding: Lunar-like (Lommel-Seeliger) law of Buratti and Mosher (1995), read in the JPL Open Repository preprint; the Icarus version was not read. Each Voyager image was fitted to I/F = f(alpha) A mu0/(mu + mu0) + (1 - A) mu0, and the paper finds that A = 1 adequately describes all observations. Its Table 1 prints f for each image. The lighting uses the clear-filter rows (0.47 micrometres, 14 to 90 degrees phase, 0.937 falling to 0.532), joined by straight lines and held beyond 90 degrees, with f = 1 at zero phase, to which the paper says f is normalized; the scan prints that angle unclearly. Flood-lit, this law is flat to the limb. The paper uses one f per image for bright and dark terrain alike. No emission range is printed; the limit 83.6 degrees is derived here from the outermost pixel of the finest image in Table 1 (9.1 km per pixel) and is second class. Squyres et al. (1984), closed, found the same lunarlike function in these images at 8 to 90 degrees phase, per its abstract.
entries.revisitWhen: A Cassini disc-resolved Iapetus law with its fitted ranges is read in the paper.

entries.subject: Shared sphere bank lighting (Lambert with a 0.35 flood floor and 0.05 ambient term, adapted from OpenSpace)
entries.finding: Replaced by the lunar-like law of Buratti and Mosher (1995); Iapetus now bakes its own bank.
entries.revisitWhen: Nothing: an authored limb is not reopened once a published law exists.

entries.subject: NASA PIA07005 Iapetus Temperature Map (Cassini CIRS, 31 December 2004 flyby)
entries.finding: Simple-cylindrical figure with a labelled frame: West Longitude 180-0 and latitude -90 to +90. Fit from the labelled frame and centre lines: 2.000 figure pixels per degree on both axes. The 10 unlabelled axis ticks (every 30 degrees) fall on the fit with 0 px residual (the half-pixel line width is 0.25 degrees). West longitude converts to east as 360 - W; the frame is 180-360 E. Landmark check against the USGS Cassini-Voyager base mosaic: along 60, 75, 105 and 120 W, the change from red to magenta (bar steps near 110 K) falls at the latitude where the mosaic brightens past gray level 140 (the Cassini Regio edge). Offsets are -5, 0, 0 and 0 degrees at the 5-degree sampling step. The color bar has 12 equal 40 px steps; its 70-130 K labels sit on every second step boundary within 2.5-5.5 px (under 0.7 K). The legend repeats those steps and labels only. Map colors are continuous rather than stepped, so pixels are shown in the published colors, not decoded to numbers. Grid lines, ticks and the subsolar asterisk are withheld as measured rectangles; each keeps a 2 px halo, since ringing beyond 2 px is under 19 RGB against at least 46 between bar steps. Background at brightest channel 19 or less (the measured halo on black) is withheld. Kept pixels cover 18.0% of the sphere. About 3% of kept pixels are paler than the bar's top step; the figure gives them no separate value. It is one moment: the Sun was overhead at the asterisk, near 106 W, 9 S.

entries.subject: NASA PIA07006 Iapetus Temperature Variation Map
entries.finding: Despite its title this is a plot, not a map: surface temperature (40-140 K) against time of day, with CIRS points and a thermal-inertia model curve. It has no latitude or longitude axis, so there is nothing to register to the surface.
entries.revisitWhen: A chart dataset is wanted and the plotted CIRS points are available as numbers from the team or an archive product.

entries.subject: Surface map left edge after the raster lane change
entries.finding: The shared raster lane writes a 0–360° E atlas, but surface-map.json still declared the retired atlas's 180° E left edge, so the globe was drawn 180° from its frame. Atlas luminance, Gazetteer craters, the source catalogue and a correlation against the georeferenced source (0.82 from 0° E, 0.21 from 180° E) all give 0° E; the declaration is now 0° E. The same source measurement found Ganymede, Ariel, Miranda, Oberon, Titania, Umbriel and Triton off by the same half turn.
